record.context_brief: Classification of perfect nonlinear one-error-correcting codes
record.original_question: Classify all perfect nonlinear single-error-correcting codes.

evidence.quote: Open Question 12.2. Classify all perfect nonlinear single error correcting codes [18].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A binary code of length $n$ is a subset $C \subseteq \mathbb{F}_2^n$. The Hamming distance $d(x,y)$ between two vectors is the number of coordinates in which they differ. A code $C$ is called a perfect single-error-correcting code (a perfect 1-error-correcting code) if the closed Hamming balls of radius $1$ centered at the codewords partition $\mathbb{F}_2^n$; equivalently, $|C| = 2^n/(n+1)$ (so $n = 2^m - 1$ for some integer $m \ge 2$) and every vector of $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ lies within Hamming distance $1$ of exactly one codeword. The code $C$ is called linear if it is an $\mathbb{F}_2$-linear subspace of $\mathbb{F}_2^n$, and nonlinear otherwise. Two codes are considered equivalent if one can be obtained from the other by a permutation of coordinates together with a translation by a fixed vector.

Problem: Provide a complete classification, up to equivalence, of all perfect nonlinear single-error-correcting binary codes (of every admissible length $n = 2^m - 1$).
artifact.status_search_result: The complete classification of perfect nonlinear single-error-correcting (binary Hamming-length) codes remains open. While linear perfect codes are completely classified (repetition, Hamming, binary/ternary Golay codes), the number of inequivalent nonlinear perfect 1-error-correcting codes grows extremely rapidly with length, and current research treats only partial invariants such as rank, kernel dimension, and connections to Steiner triple systems and tilings. Surveys of perfect codes describe full classification as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: A survey of perfect codes
status_evidence.snippet: Recent results on perfect 1-error correcting binary codes... constructions, classification by rank and kernel dimension...
status_evidence.claim: Classification of perfect nonlinear 1-error-correcting binary codes is studied only via partial invariants; a full classification is not known.

status_evidence.title: Survey of the methods for constructing nonlinear perfect binary codes
status_evidence.snippet: Methods for constructing nonlinear perfect binary codes are surveyed, indicating a vast and not fully classified family.
status_evidence.claim: Many constructions of nonlinear perfect binary codes exist, but a complete classification is not available.

status_evidence.title: Perfect code | Error Correction Zoo
status_evidence.snippet: Lists perfect codes and notes the abundance of nonlinear single-error-correcting perfect codes.
status_evidence.claim: The set of nonlinear perfect 1-error-correcting codes is very large and not fully classified.
